generic.Defined scope/population: All customers holding an in-force or recently lapsed policy in the lines agreed for segmentation.
generic.In-scope period: Rolling 36-month window of policy, billing, CRM, and portal behaviour ending at the extract date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Customer master ID, tenure, premium, product holding, and channel populated on every customer row.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Customer count and in-force premium reconcile to the policy admin in-force report within 0.5%.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Extract scripts, run log, and reconciliation sheet retained with run timestamp and dataset version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Orphan and unmatched policy records logged in the data quality tool with owner and fix decision.
generic.Test population: The assembled unified customer dataset in the segmentation staging schema for the current build.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass at reconciliation variance under 0.5% and zero unmasked restricted PII columns.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst refers the defect to the source data steward and reruns the extract before sign-off.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Dataset reconciled, PII masked, catalog entry complete, and refresh job documented.
generic.Evidence location: Segmentation staging schema plus the catalog entry and reconciliation pack in the analytics workspace.

steps.title: Confirm the source table list and 36-month window in the data catalog
sop: Open the data catalog and list the policy, billing, CRM, and portal behaviour tables needed for segmentation.
Record the certified source table for each domain and note the owner and refresh frequency shown in the catalog.
Fix the extract window at the agreed rolling 36 months ending at the current extract date.
Done when the source table list and window are recorded in the build notes.
verify: Check every listed source table is catalog-certified rather than an ad hoc copy.
Pass when all four source domains have a named certified table and an agreed extract window.

steps.title: Extract the source tables into the segmentation staging schema in the lakehouse
sop: Run the extract job that loads policy, billing, CRM, and behavioural tables into the segmentation staging schema.
Record the run timestamp, source snapshot date, and row count landed for each table in the run log.
Rerun any table whose load fails rather than proceeding on a partial extract.
Done when all staged tables are loaded and row counts are logged.
verify: Compare the staged row counts to the source system counts for the same window.
Pass when every staged table matches its source count and the run log is complete.

steps.title: Join the staged tables on customer master ID in the lakehouse
sop: Join the staged tables on the customer master ID rather than the policy number.
Collapse multi-policy households onto a single customer row and aggregate policy-level fields up to customer level.
List any policy row that fails to resolve to a customer master ID and hold it for exception handling.
Done when one row per customer exists in the unified dataset.
verify: Check the dataset has no duplicate customer master ID and no policy-level duplication of premium.
Pass when the customer key is unique across the whole unified dataset.

steps.title: Reconcile customer count and in-force premium to the policy admin report
sop: Pull the in-force report from the policy administration system for the same as-of date.
Compare unified dataset customer count and in-force premium to the report and calculate the variance.
Investigate and explain any variance above 0.5% before the dataset is released.
Done when the reconciliation sheet is completed and saved with the build.
verify: Recompute the variance from the reconciliation sheet figures.
Pass when both customer count and premium variance are under 0.5% or fully explained.

steps.title: Mask or drop restricted PII columns from the segmentation extract
sop: Scan the unified dataset column list against the restricted field list covering SSN, full DOB, and bank details.
Drop or mask every restricted column and record the treatment applied to each.
Confirm the analyst-facing view exposes only the approved column set.
Done when no unmasked restricted field remains readable in the segmentation extract.
verify: Query the analyst-facing view for each restricted field name and inspect the returned values.
Pass when no restricted field returns unmasked values to a segmentation analyst account.

steps.title: Register the unified dataset in the data catalog and log exceptions
sop: Create the catalog entry with owner, steward, classification, refresh frequency, and source lineage.
Attach the reconciliation sheet and the column treatment record to the catalog entry.
Log every unresolved orphan or match failure in the data quality tool with an owner and due date.
Done when the catalog entry is published and all exceptions carry an owner.
verify: Open the catalog entry and confirm owner, steward, classification, and refresh frequency are populated.
Pass when the Customer Insights Lead confirms the entry is complete and every exception is dispositioned.

generic.Defined scope/population: The prepared segmentation feature set for all in-scope customers used to fit the clustering model.
generic.In-scope period: The training snapshot date for the current segmentation build cycle.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Chosen k, hyperparameters, random seed, and snapshot date populated in the model record.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Training row count in the model run matches the prepared feature table row count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Model artefact, scoring script, and tuning results stored under a dated version in the model repository.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Segments breaching the 40% or 3% size bounds logged with the retune decision taken.
generic.Test population: A random holdout of customers scored with the tuned model for the current build.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when holdout cluster assignment is stable and no segment exceeds ~40% or falls below ~3%.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst retunes k or the feature scaling and reruns before the model is registered.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Tuned model registered with hyperparameters, seed, snapshot date, and stability evidence.
generic.Evidence location: Model governance repository version record plus the tuning workbook in the analytics workspace.

steps.title: Load the prepared feature table into the modelling session on the lakehouse
sop: Point the modelling session at the versioned prepared feature table in the lakehouse.
Record the feature table version, snapshot date, and row count used for training.
Confirm the feature list matches the approved variable dictionary before fitting.
Done when the training input is loaded and its version recorded.
verify: Compare the loaded feature list to the approved variable dictionary entry by entry.
Pass when the loaded features and row count match the approved dictionary and feature table version.

steps.title: Run the candidate k sweep and capture silhouette and within-cluster metrics
sop: Fit the clustering model across the agreed candidate k range using a fixed random seed.
Capture silhouette score and within-cluster sum of squares for each candidate k in the tuning workbook.
Plot both measures so the elbow and peak silhouette are visible to a reviewer.
Done when every candidate k has recorded metrics in the tuning workbook.
verify: Check the tuning workbook has a metric row for every k in the candidate range.
Pass when no candidate k is missing a silhouette and within-cluster value.

steps.title: Select the chosen k and record the rationale in the tuning workbook
sop: Select the k that balances silhouette, within-cluster fit, and business interpretability.
Write the selection rationale including why neighbouring k values were rejected.
Review the chosen k with the Customer Insights Lead before proceeding to stability testing.
Done when the chosen k and rationale are recorded and reviewed.
verify: Read the rationale against the recorded metrics for the chosen and neighbouring k values.
Pass when the Customer Insights Lead accepts the chosen k and the stated rationale.

steps.title: Re-run the tuned model on a random holdout to test assignment stability
sop: Draw a random holdout of customers and score them with the tuned model.
Compare holdout cluster assignments against the full-population assignments and measure the agreement rate.
Record the stability result and the holdout size in the tuning workbook.
Done when the stability comparison is complete and recorded.
verify: Recompute the agreement rate from the recorded holdout comparison table.
Pass when the stability rate meets the agreed minimum for the build.

steps.title: Check segment size distribution against the 40% and 3% bounds in Excel
sop: Produce the segment size table showing customer count and share of base for each cluster.
Flag any segment above roughly 40% or below roughly 3% of the customer base.
Retune k or the feature scaling and rerun when a bound is breached, logging the decision taken.
Done when all segments sit within the agreed size bounds or the breach is logged and accepted.
verify: Sum the segment shares and check each share against the upper and lower bounds.
Pass when shares total 100% and no unlogged bound breach remains.

steps.title: Register the tuned model artefact in the model governance repository
sop: Create a new model version in the governance repository for the tuned segmentation model.
Upload the model artefact, scoring script, tuning workbook, and stability results to that version.
Record final hyperparameters, chosen k, random seed, and training snapshot date on the version record.
Done when the version record is complete and the artefacts are attached.
verify: Open the new version record and confirm artefact, script, hyperparameters, seed, and snapshot date are present.
Pass when the Customer Insights Lead confirms the version record is complete and reproducible.

generic.Defined scope/population: The customer population segmentation will cover, stating personal lines, commercial lines, or both.
generic.In-scope period: The current planning cycle in which the segmentation will be built and activated.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every business question carries a named requesting owner, an activation route, and a success measure.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Question count in the approved note matches the questions raised by marketing, distribution, and product.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Dated and versioned objectives note retained in the team workspace with the sign-off thread.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Questions deferred or ruled out of scope logged with the reason and the deciding owner.
generic.Test population: The approved segmentation objectives and approach note for the current cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every question has a named owner and written sign-off is held from all three teams.
generic.Exception handling path: Customer Insights Lead reopens the note and recirculates when a stakeholder withholds sign-off.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Objectives, in-scope population, exclusion rules, activation routes, and success measures all documented.
generic.Evidence location: Segmentation objectives note in SharePoint with the Confluence page and sign-off emails attached.

steps.title: Collect the business questions from marketing and distribution in Teams sessions
sop: Run working sessions with marketing, distribution, and product to collect the questions segmentation must answer.
Capture each question covering targeting, retention, pricing tiering, and channel fit as a separate entry.
Name the requesting owner against every question captured.
Done when the question list is captured with an owner on each entry.
verify: Read the question list and check each entry has a single named requester.
Pass when no question is recorded without a named requesting owner.

steps.title: Agree the in-scope population and exclusion rules with the requesting teams
sop: Agree whether personal lines, commercial lines, or both are in scope for this segmentation.
Agree the exclusion rules for lapsed, non-renewed, and non-customer prospect records.
Record the population and exclusion decisions in the objectives note draft.
Done when the in-scope population and exclusions are written into the draft.
verify: Check the draft states the population and every exclusion rule explicitly.
Pass when the population statement leaves no line of business ambiguous.

steps.title: Agree how segments will be activated with the Marketing Manager
sop: State how segments will actually be used across campaign targeting, producer prioritisation, and product design.
Confirm the activation route for each use so the segmentation design fits the way it will be consumed.
Flag any activation route that the current campaign or CRM tooling cannot support.
Done when every intended activation route is documented in the draft note.
verify: Trace each business question in the draft to a stated activation route.
Pass when every question maps to an activation route that the tooling can support.

steps.title: Define success measures and baselines for the segmentation in Excel
sop: Define the success measures such as campaign response lift and segment stability over 12 months.
Record the current baseline value for each measure so improvement can be evidenced later.
Note the data source and owner for each success measure.
Done when every success measure has a baseline and a source recorded.
verify: Check each success measure has a baseline value and a named data source.
Pass when no success measure is listed without a baseline.

steps.title: Draft the objectives and approach note in SharePoint
sop: Assemble the questions, population, exclusions, activation routes, and success measures into one note.
Summarise the intended approach and the expected delivery dates against the planning calendar.
Version and date the note and publish it to the team workspace for review.
Done when the versioned draft note is published for review.
verify: Check the note contains all five content sections and carries a version and date.
Pass when no required section is missing from the published draft.

steps.title: Circulate the note for written sign-off from marketing, distribution, and product
sop: Send the note to the marketing, distribution, and product leads with a stated response date.
Log every comment received and record whether it was accepted, adjusted, or declined.
Reissue the note when material changes are made and seek sign-off again.
Done when written sign-off is held from all three teams.
verify: Check the sign-off thread contains an explicit approval from each of the three teams.
Pass when the Marketing Manager confirms all three approvals are recorded against the final version.

generic.Defined scope/population: Candidate variables across demographics, tenure, value, product holding, claims, and engagement.
generic.In-scope period: The observation windows applied to the current segmentation build snapshot.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every dictionary entry carries source table, column, transformation, and glossary term.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Variable count in the published dictionary matches the approved clustering variable list.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Variable dictionary versioned and dated in the catalog with the exclusion rationale attached.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Variables failing the populated-rate test logged with the drop or impute decision recorded.
generic.Test population: The published segmentation variable dictionary for the current build.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every variable is at or above 95% populated and no protected characteristic appears.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst drops or imputes the failing variable and records the treatment before publication.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Dictionary published with lineage, scaling rule, distance measure, and exclusion rationale.
generic.Evidence location: Data catalog dictionary entry with the supporting profiling workbook in the analytics workspace.

steps.title: Draft the candidate variable list from the lakehouse customer tables
sop: List candidate variables across demographics, tenure, premium value, product holding, claims, and engagement.
Record the source table and column in the lakehouse for each candidate variable.
Group the candidates by domain so coverage gaps are visible.
Done when the candidate list is drafted with source lineage on each entry.
verify: Check each candidate variable resolves to a real source table and column.
Pass when every candidate has a valid source table and column reference.

steps.title: Run the protected characteristic and proxy exclusion test on the candidate list
sop: Test each candidate against the protected characteristic list and the known proxy list.
Remove protected characteristics and close proxies such as ZIP-only demographic indicators.
Record the reason for each exclusion so the decision can be evidenced later.
Done when the exclusion test is complete and every removal is documented.
verify: Re-scan the remaining variable list against the protected characteristic and proxy lists.
Pass when no protected characteristic or listed proxy remains on the variable list.

steps.title: Profile populated rates for each candidate variable in the data quality tool
sop: Profile each candidate variable and record its populated rate over the segmentation population.
Apply the minimum populated rate of 95% and mark variables that fail.
Decide drop or impute for each failing variable and record the treatment and its rationale.
Done when every candidate carries a populated rate and a keep, drop, or impute decision.
verify: Check the profiling output lists a populated rate for every candidate variable.
Pass when no retained variable sits below the 95% threshold without a recorded imputation.

steps.title: Set the distance measure and scaling rule for continuous variables
sop: Select the clustering distance measure appropriate to the retained variable types.
Set the standardisation or scaling rule applied to continuous variables before clustering.
Record both decisions with the reasoning in the model documentation.
Done when the distance measure and scaling rule are documented.
verify: Check the documented scaling rule covers every retained continuous variable.
Pass when no continuous variable enters clustering without a stated scaling treatment.

steps.title: Review the retained variable list with the Customer Insights Lead
sop: Walk the retained variable list and the exclusions through with the Data Analyst.
Challenge any variable that cannot be explained to a marketing or distribution audience.
Record accepted, removed, and added variables from the review.
Done when the retained list is agreed and the review outcome recorded.
verify: Check the review record shows a decision against every challenged variable.
Pass when the Customer Insights Lead confirms the retained list is agreed.

steps.title: Publish the variable dictionary to the data catalog
sop: Publish the final dictionary with source table, column, transformation, and glossary term per entry.
Attach the exclusion rationale and the profiling workbook to the catalog entry.
Version and date the dictionary so later builds can be compared against it.
Done when the dictionary is published and linked to the segmentation dataset entry.
verify: Open the published dictionary and check lineage and glossary links on a sample of entries.
Pass when every sampled entry has complete lineage and a resolvable glossary link.

generic.Defined scope/population: All in-scope customers in the prepared attribute set receiving behavioural, value, and risk features.
generic.In-scope period: Rolling 3, 12, and 36-month feature windows ending at the build snapshot date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every customer row carries populated behavioural, value, and risk features or a documented default.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Feature table row count matches the prepared customer attribute set row count exactly.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Feature build script committed to version control with the reviewer and build date recorded.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Winsorised outliers and dropped correlated features logged with the threshold applied.
generic.Test population: The built segmentation feature table for the current snapshot.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when no retained feature pair exceeds the agreed correlation limit and row counts match.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst drops one of the correlated pair or re-caps the outlier and reruns the build.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Feature table built with documented window definitions and a peer-reviewed build script.
generic.Evidence location: Feature table in the lakehouse with the build script in version control and the review record attached.

steps.title: Build behavioural features over 3, 12, and 36-month windows in Snowflake
sop: Build portal login, service contact, and digital quote activity counts for each customer.
Compute each behavioural feature over the rolling 3, 12, and 36-month windows.
Record the exact window definition and the anchor date used for each feature.
Done when all behavioural features exist for all three windows.
verify: Recompute one behavioural feature for a sample customer directly from the source event table.
Pass when the sampled recomputation matches the feature table value.

steps.title: Build value features from premium and tenure in the lakehouse
sop: Compute earned premium, loss ratio contribution, tenure, and product count per customer.
Aggregate policy-level premium correctly to customer level for multi-policy households.
Record the definition and source of each value feature in the feature dictionary.
Done when all value features are built at customer level.
verify: Reconcile total earned premium across the feature table to the source premium table.
Pass when total earned premium reconciles within the agreed tolerance.

steps.title: Build customer-level risk features from claims history
sop: Compute claim frequency and severity history at customer level rather than policy level.
Roll claims across all policies held by the same customer master ID.
Record the claims observation window used for the risk features.
Done when frequency and severity features exist for every customer row.
verify: Check a multi-policy customer aggregates claims from every policy held.
Pass when the sampled customer risk features include all their policy claims.

steps.title: Cap or winsorise premium and claim amount outliers at the agreed percentile
sop: Inspect the distribution of premium and claim amount features for extreme values.
Apply the agreed winsorisation percentile to cap outliers on both features.
Record the threshold values applied and the number of rows affected.
Done when caps are applied and the thresholds and affected counts are logged.
verify: Check the maximum value of each capped feature against the recorded threshold.
Pass when no capped feature exceeds its recorded threshold value.

steps.title: Run the correlation check and drop redundant features in Excel
sop: Produce the pairwise correlation matrix across all engineered features.
Identify every pair correlated above the agreed threshold and drop one feature from each pair.
Record which feature was dropped from each pair and why it was the weaker choice.
Done when no retained feature pair breaches the correlation threshold.
verify: Re-run the correlation matrix on the retained feature set only.
Pass when the retained matrix shows no pair above the agreed threshold.

steps.title: Peer-review the feature build script and commit it to version control
sop: Review the feature build script against the documented window and transformation definitions.
Raise findings on any undocumented transformation or hard-coded value in the script.
Record the review outcome and commit the reviewed script to version control.
Done when the reviewed script is committed with the reviewer named.
verify: Open the version control record and check the reviewer and review date are present.
Pass when the committed script carries a completed review record.

generic.Defined scope/population: All published segments monitored for size drift against their baseline at model build.
generic.In-scope period: Quarterly drift checks running until the next scheduled annual model refresh date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Baseline share, current share, threshold, and named owner populated for every segment.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Current segment shares in the monitoring view sum to 100% of the scored customer base.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Each quarterly drift check retained with run date and the model version it compares against.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Segments breaching the drift threshold logged with the investigation outcome recorded.
generic.Test population: The live segment stability monitoring view in the BI platform.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when drift beyond 5 percentage points on any segment raises a flag and an escalation.
generic.Exception handling path: Customer Insights Lead investigates the breach and decides whether to bring the refresh forward.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Drift view live with documented thresholds, cadence, escalation path, and annual refresh date.
generic.Evidence location: BI monitoring view plus the cadence document in SharePoint and the model repository record.

steps.title: Capture the baseline segment size distribution from the model build
sop: Extract the segment size distribution recorded at model build from the model governance repository.
Store the baseline shares as the fixed comparison point for drift monitoring.
Record the model version and build date the baseline belongs to.
Done when the baseline distribution is stored against the model version.
verify: Check the stored baseline shares sum to 100% and match the model build record.
Pass when the baseline matches the repository record for the approved model version.

steps.title: Set the drift threshold and quarterly check cadence
sop: Set the drift threshold that triggers investigation at any segment shifting more than 5 percentage points.
Set the check cadence at quarterly and fix the check dates against the reporting calendar.
Name the owner responsible for running each quarterly check.
Done when the threshold, cadence, and owner are agreed and recorded.
verify: Check the recorded threshold and cadence are stated in measurable terms.
Pass when the threshold, cadence dates, and named owner are all recorded.

steps.title: Build the segment stability monitoring view in the BI platform
sop: Build the view showing baseline share, current share, and the point difference for every segment.
Add a visual flag that fires when a segment exceeds the drift threshold.
Display the data as-of date on the view so stale refreshes are visible.
Done when the view renders every segment with baseline, current, and drift flag.
verify: Open the view and check the drift flag fires on a test segment breaching the threshold.
Pass when the flag fires correctly and the as-of date displays.

steps.title: Publish the monitoring view to the marketing analytics workspace
sop: Publish the stability view into the marketing analytics workspace in the BI platform.
Grant view access to marketing, distribution, and the insights team.
Confirm an end user in each team can open the view without a permission error.
Done when the view is published and accessible to all three teams.
verify: Open the view under a marketing user account and a distribution user account.
Pass when both accounts render the view with current data.

steps.title: Schedule the annual model refresh in the model governance repository
sop: Set the annual segmentation model refresh date on the model repository record.
Name the owner accountable for delivering the refresh on that date.
Add the refresh to the team planning calendar so capacity is reserved.
Done when the refresh date and owner are recorded on the model record.
verify: Open the model record and check the next refresh date and owner are populated.
Pass when the refresh date is in the calendar and the model record agrees with it.

steps.title: Document the drift escalation path in SharePoint
sop: Write the escalation path taken when drift breaches the threshold between scheduled refreshes.
State who investigates, who decides on an early refresh, and the response timescale.
Publish the cadence and escalation document alongside the monitoring view link.
Done when the escalation path is published and linked from the monitoring view.
verify: Read the published document and confirm it names the investigator and the decision maker.
Pass when the escalation path names roles and timescales rather than teams alone.

generic.Defined scope/population: All customer records in the unified dataset subject to match, merge, and third-party enrichment.
generic.In-scope period: The current segmentation build snapshot with third-party attributes at their licensed refresh date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Standardised address and contact fields populated before matching runs on every record.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Golden record count plus merged duplicates equals the pre-merge customer record count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Match rules, merge results, and vendor licence records retained with the run date and version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every data quality exception logged in the issue tracker with an owner and due date.
generic.Test population: The prepared customer attribute set produced by the current preparation run.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every appended attribute meets the agreed populated rate and holds a licence record.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst rejects the failing attribute and refers unresolved matches to the data steward.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Deduplicated attribute set with field-level completeness profile and vendor licence evidence.
generic.Evidence location: Prepared attribute set in the lakehouse with the profile and licence records in the data catalog.

steps.title: Standardise address and contact fields in the lakehouse before matching
sop: Apply the address standardisation routine to every customer address in the unified dataset.
Normalise phone and email formats so near-duplicates become comparable.
Record the count of records changed by standardisation.
Done when all address and contact fields are standardised.
verify: Sample standardised addresses and compare them to the raw source values.
Pass when the sampled records show correct and non-destructive standardisation.

steps.title: Run the match and merge rules to build golden customer records
sop: Run the agreed match rules to identify duplicate customer and household records.
Merge matched records into one golden record per customer using the survivorship rules.
Record the number of records merged and the number left as unresolved possible matches.
Done when the golden record set is produced with merge counts logged.
verify: Check golden record count plus merged duplicates equals the pre-merge record count.
Pass when the record count reconciliation balances exactly.

steps.title: Review a sample of merges and near-matches with the Customer Insights Lead
sop: Review a sample of merged records and a sample of rejected near-matches.
Confirm merges combined the same customer and not two similar customers.
Record any false merge found and refer it back for rule adjustment.
Done when the sample review is complete and findings are recorded.
verify: Count false merges found in the reviewed sample against the acceptable tolerance.
Pass when false merges in the sample sit at or below the agreed tolerance.

steps.title: Append licensed third-party demographic attributes and record the licence terms
sop: Append the licensed demographic and lifestyle attributes to the golden records.
Record the vendor, licence reference, and permitted-use terms for each appended attribute.
Confirm the permitted use covers segmentation and internal marketing activation.
Done when every appended attribute carries a vendor and licence record.
verify: Check each appended attribute has a vendor licence record with permitted-use terms.
Pass when no appended attribute lacks a current licence record.

steps.title: Profile field-level completeness in the data quality tool
sop: Profile the prepared attribute set and record the populated rate for every field.
Reject any attribute falling below the agreed populated rate and record the rejection.
Publish the completeness profile alongside the prepared attribute set.
Done when the profile is published and failing attributes are removed.
verify: Check the published profile lists a populated rate for every retained field.
Pass when no retained field sits below the agreed populated rate.

steps.title: Log data quality exceptions in the issue tracker with owners
sop: Raise each unresolved match failure, missing attribute, and source defect as a tracked issue.
Assign a named owner and a due date to every issue raised.
Link the issues to the prepared attribute set catalog entry so they stay visible.
Done when every exception found during preparation is tracked with an owner.
verify: Filter the issue tracker for this preparation run and inspect each entry.
Pass when no exception is recorded without an owner and a due date.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every segment produced by the approved clustering run for the current model version.
generic.In-scope period: The scoring snapshot the segment membership and value figures were derived from.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Size, average premium, product holding, tenure, retention, and loss ratio populated per segment.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Segment sizes in the profile pack sum to the total scored customer population.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Profile pack published with the model version, snapshot date, and pack version stamped on it.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Segments with unstable or implausible profile metrics logged with the action taken.
generic.Test population: The published segment profile pack covering all segments in the current model version.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every segment has a plain business name, a persona page, and a value estimate.
generic.Exception handling path: Customer Insights Lead sends the segment back for renaming or reprofiling before publication.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Named segments with size, value, lifetime value, and persona narrative for every segment.
generic.Evidence location: Segment profile pack in the marketing workspace with the BI profile report linked.

steps.title: Build the segment profile table in the BI platform
sop: Build the profile table showing size, average premium, product holding, tenure, retention, and loss ratio per segment.
Stamp the table with the model version and scoring snapshot date used.
Check segment sizes sum to the total scored population before sharing.
Done when the profile table renders complete metrics for every segment.
verify: Sum the segment sizes and compare to the total scored customer count.
Pass when the sizes reconcile and no metric cell is blank.

steps.title: Estimate average and lifetime customer value per segment in Excel
sop: Calculate average customer value per segment from earned premium and margin inputs.
Calculate expected lifetime value per segment using the published retention curve.
Record the assumptions behind both figures on the face of the calculation.
Done when both value figures exist for every segment with assumptions stated.
verify: Recompute the value figures for one segment from the stated inputs.
Pass when the recomputed figures match the published values.

steps.title: Write the one-page persona narrative for each segment
sop: Write a one-page persona per segment covering needs, channel preference, and typical product mix.
Ground each persona statement in the profile metrics rather than assumption.
Flag any persona claim that the data does not support and remove it.
Done when every segment has a persona page grounded in its profile metrics.
verify: Trace three claims per persona back to the underlying profile metric.
Pass when every traced claim is supported by a profile metric.

steps.title: Assign plain business names to each segment
sop: Replace every numeric cluster label with a plain business name that describes the segment.
Check each name is neutral and non-pejorative about the customers it describes.
Confirm the names are understandable to marketing and distribution without explanation.
Done when no segment carries a numeric cluster label.
verify: Scan the profile pack for any remaining cluster number used as a label.
Pass when no numeric cluster label appears anywhere in the pack.

steps.title: Assemble the segment profile pack in SharePoint
sop: Combine the profile table, value estimates, and persona pages into a single pack.
Add the model version, snapshot date, and pack version to the cover page.
Add a contents page so a reader can find any segment quickly.
Done when the pack is assembled with version and source stamps on the cover.
verify: Check the pack contains a profile page and a persona page for every segment.
Pass when no segment is missing either page.

steps.title: Publish the profile pack to the marketing workspace
sop: Publish the pack to the marketing workspace and notify marketing and distribution.
Link the pack to the model version record so its provenance is traceable.
Retire the previous profile pack from the live folder at publication.
Done when the pack is live and the prior version is retired.
verify: Open the marketing workspace and check only the current pack is live.
Pass when the current pack opens and no superseded pack sits alongside it.

generic.Defined scope/population: All scored customers whose segment code is published onto the CRM customer record.
generic.In-scope period: The current segment scoring run and the recurring refresh cycle that follows it.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Segment code and segment name populated on every scored CRM customer record.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: CRM scored record count reconciles to the segmentation output within 0.5%.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Load run log, reconciliation record, and refresh job schedule retained with the run date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Customer records failing to load into CRM logged with the cause and resolution.
generic.Test population: CRM customer records loaded in the current segment publication run.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass at load variance under 0.5% and zero restricted PII fields in the publication feed.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst investigates the variance and reloads failed records before sign-off.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Segment field populated and read-only in CRM with a scheduled refresh proven to run.
generic.Evidence location: CRM customer records plus the load run log and reconciliation record in the lakehouse.

steps.title: Map segment code and name to the controlled CRM customer fields
sop: Map the segment code and segment name from the output table to the CRM customer fields.
Confirm the target fields are the controlled segmentation fields and not free-text fields.
Confirm no account number or restricted PII column is included in the feed mapping.
Done when the field mapping is agreed and the feed excludes restricted fields.
verify: Review the feed column list against the restricted field list.
Pass when the feed carries only segment code, name, and the customer key.

steps.title: Load the segment feed into CRM in the sandbox first
sop: Run the segment load into the CRM sandbox against a representative sample of customers.
Check the loaded values render on the customer record as expected.
Fix any mapping or format defect before running the production load.
Done when the sandbox load completes cleanly on the sample.
verify: Open sampled sandbox customer records and inspect the segment fields.
Pass when the sampled records show the correct segment code and name.

steps.title: Run the production segment load into CRM
sop: Run the production load of segment code and name onto the CRM customer records.
Record the run date, source output version, and records loaded and failed.
Reload failed records after fixing the cause rather than leaving them unscored.
Done when the production load completes and failures are resolved or logged.
verify: Read the load run log for loaded, failed, and reloaded record counts.
Pass when no failed record remains unresolved and unlogged.

steps.title: Reconcile CRM scored counts to the segmentation output
sop: Count customers holding a segment code in CRM and compare to the segmentation output count.
Calculate the variance and investigate anything above 0.5%.
Record the reconciliation result with the run date.
Done when the reconciliation is recorded and any variance explained.
verify: Recompute the variance from the recorded counts.
Pass when the variance is under 0.5% or fully explained in the record.

steps.title: Set the segment field to read-only for marketing and distribution users
sop: Set the CRM field-level security so marketing and distribution users can view but not edit the segment field.
Confirm the field appears on the customer page layouts those users work from.
Test the permission with a marketing user profile and a distribution user profile.
Done when both profiles can read the field and neither can edit it.
verify: Attempt to edit the segment field under a marketing user profile.
Pass when the edit is blocked and the value remains visible.

steps.title: Schedule the recurring segment refresh job and confirm the first run
sop: Schedule the recurring segment refresh from the lakehouse into CRM at the agreed frequency.
Set failure alerting so a missed refresh notifies the Data Analyst.
Wait for the first scheduled run and confirm it completes successfully.
Done when the first scheduled refresh completes and alerting is active.
verify: Read the scheduler history for the first completed run and the alert configuration.
Pass when the first run shows success and failure alerting is enabled.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every customer in the current prepared attribute set submitted to the approved clustering model.
generic.In-scope period: The input snapshot date of the prepared customer attribute set used for this run.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Run date, model version, input snapshot, and record count populated in the run log.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Segment membership row count equals the prepared attribute set row count exactly.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Run log and membership output retained in the governed analytics schema with the run date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Unassigned or failed records logged with the cause and the rerun or exclusion decision.
generic.Test population: The segment membership output table produced by the current clustering run.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when zero customers are unassigned and segment size movement stays within tolerance.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst reruns the failed partition or escalates the tolerance breach to the Lead.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Membership output stored in the governed schema with a complete run log entry.
generic.Evidence location: Governed analytics schema membership table with the run log entry attached.

steps.title: Confirm the approved model version in the model governance repository
sop: Open the model governance repository and identify the currently approved segmentation model version.
Confirm the scoring script referenced matches that approved version.
Record the model version to be used in the run log.
Done when the approved model version is confirmed and recorded.
verify: Compare the scoring script version against the approved repository version.
Pass when the script and the approved model version match exactly.

steps.title: Execute the clustering model against the prepared attribute set in Snowflake
sop: Run the approved clustering model against the current prepared customer attribute set.
Capture the job status and any partition failures during execution.
Rerun failed partitions rather than accepting a partial result.
Done when the clustering job completes across the whole population.
verify: Read the job status and check for partition failures.
Pass when the job reports success across all partitions.

steps.title: Record the run details in the clustering run log
sop: Record the run date, model version, input snapshot date, and input record count in the run log.
Record the output record count and the number of segments produced.
Link the run log entry to the model governance version record.
Done when the run log entry is complete and linked.
verify: Open the run log entry and check every field is populated.
Pass when no run log field is left blank for this run.

steps.title: Check every customer has a segment assignment in the membership table
sop: Count rows in the membership table with a null or missing segment assignment.
Investigate the cause of any unassigned record and reprocess it where possible.
Log any record left unassigned with the reason it could not be scored.
Done when no unassigned record remains without a logged reason.
verify: Query the membership table for null segment assignments.
Pass when the query returns zero rows or every returned row has a logged reason.

steps.title: Compare segment sizes against the previous run in Excel
sop: Build the comparison of current segment sizes against the previous run.
Flag any segment moving more than the agreed tolerance between runs.
Write a short explanation for each flagged movement.
Done when the comparison is complete and flagged movements are explained.
verify: Check each flagged segment carries a written explanation.
Pass when no flagged movement is left unexplained.

steps.title: Store the membership output in the governed analytics schema
sop: Write the segment membership output into the governed analytics schema, not a local drive.
Apply the standard access controls to the output table.
Notify the Customer Insights Lead that the run output is available.
Done when the output is stored in the governed schema and access is set.
verify: Confirm the output table exists in the governed schema with the expected access controls.
Pass when the Customer Insights Lead can open the table and the run log entry.

generic.Defined scope/population: The candidate clustering methods considered for this segmentation build.
generic.In-scope period: The current segmentation design cycle before feature engineering begins.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each candidate method carries a score on interpretability, stability, and data-type fit.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Every candidate method listed at the start appears in the final comparison with a decision.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Dated methodology decision recorded in the model documentation with the reviewer named.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Rejected methods logged with the specific reason each was not selected.
generic.Test population: The recorded methodology decision and its comparison of candidate methods.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when the chosen method is supported by approved tooling and has a named reviewer.
generic.Exception handling path: Data Analyst reopens the comparison when the reviewer challenges the selection.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Decision recorded with the option comparison, rejection reasons, and reviewer name.
generic.Evidence location: Model documentation page in Confluence with the comparison workbook in SharePoint.

steps.title: List the candidate clustering methods in the comparison workbook
sop: List the candidate methods covering k-means, hierarchical, latent class, and RFM-style rules.
Note the data types and assumptions each method requires.
Set up the comparison workbook with a row per candidate method.
Done when every candidate method has a row in the comparison workbook.
verify: Check the workbook covers all four candidate method families.
Pass when no candidate family is missing from the comparison.

steps.title: Score each method on interpretability, stability, and data-type fit
sop: Score each candidate against interpretability, stability, and fit to the segmentation variable types.
Write the reasoning behind each score rather than recording a bare number.
Highlight where a method conflicts with the mixed variable types in the dictionary.
Done when every candidate carries a scored and reasoned assessment.
verify: Check each score has supporting reasoning in the workbook.
Pass when no score is recorded without reasoning.

steps.title: Confirm the shortlisted method is explainable to a non-statistical audience
sop: Test whether the shortlisted method can be explained to marketing and distribution without statistics training.
Draft the plain-language explanation that would be given to those teams.
Reject the shortlist and reconsider when the explanation cannot be made simply.
Done when a plain-language explanation of the chosen method exists.
verify: Read the plain-language explanation for jargon and unexplained terms.
Pass when the explanation stands without statistical vocabulary.

steps.title: Confirm the chosen method is supported by the approved analytics tooling
sop: Check the chosen method is implementable in the approved analytics tooling used for scheduled runs.
Confirm the method can be rerun on the agreed refresh cadence without manual steps.
Record any tooling limitation that constrains the implementation.
Done when tooling support for the chosen method is confirmed and recorded.
verify: Check the tooling confirmation names the specific platform and job type used.
Pass when the method is proven runnable on the scheduled platform.

steps.title: Record the rejected options and the reason each was not selected
sop: Record each rejected method with the specific reason it was not selected.
Distinguish rejections on interpretability from rejections on tooling or data fit.
Keep the rejection record with the comparison workbook for future rebuilds.
Done when every rejected method has a recorded reason.
verify: Check every non-selected method carries a rejection reason.
Pass when no rejected method is recorded without a reason.

steps.title: Log the methodology decision in the model documentation
sop: Write the methodology decision into the model documentation page.
Record the decision date, the decision maker, and the reviewer name.
Link the comparison workbook to the documentation page.
Done when the decision is logged with date, decision maker, and reviewer.
verify: Open the documentation page and check date, decision maker, and reviewer are recorded.
Pass when all three fields are populated and the workbook link resolves.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every published segment reviewed against distribution and product team business needs.
generic.In-scope period: The validation window before the segmentation is released for targeting use.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each segment has a stated planned use, an actionability verdict, and a channel volume check.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Number of segments reviewed matches the number of segments in the published profile pack.

generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every challenge raised logged with an accept, adjust, or defer decision and its rationale.
generic.Test population: The signed validation record covering all segments in the current model version.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every segment is judged actionable and both leads have signed off in writing.
generic.Exception handling path: Customer Insights Lead refers segments judged unactionable back for reprofiling or retuning.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Written sign-off from distribution and product with all challenges dispositioned.
generic.Evidence location: Validation record in SharePoint with the BI profile report and sign-off emails attached.

steps.title: Circulate the segment profile pack to distribution and product ahead of the session
sop: Send the profile pack to distribution and product leads with the review date and agenda.
Ask each team to come with field observations against the segments they recognise.
Confirm attendance from both teams before the session.
Done when the pack is circulated and both teams have confirmed attendance.
verify: Check the circulation record shows both teams received the pack in advance.
Pass when both leads confirm receipt before the review date.

steps.title: Walk each segment profile through with the distribution team
sop: Walk each segment profile through and ask whether it matches what producers see in the field.
Capture where the field view differs from the profile and by how much.
Note segments the field does not recognise at all.
Done when every segment has a recorded field-recognition response.
verify: Check every segment has a field response recorded against it.
Pass when no segment is left without a field-recognition response.

steps.title: Test each segment against a real planned use in the BI platform
sop: Take each segment and test it against a real planned use such as a campaign target or producer priority list.
Confirm the segment can actually be selected and actioned in that route.
Record an actionable or not-actionable verdict for each segment.
Done when every segment carries an actionability verdict.
verify: Check each verdict names the specific planned use it was tested against.
Pass when every segment verdict cites a named planned use.

steps.title: Confirm segment sizes support planned campaign volumes per channel
sop: Compare each segment size against the campaign volume planned for it in each channel.
Flag segments too small to support the planned activity in a channel.
Record the required minimum volume against each flagged segment.
Done when every segment has a volume sufficiency check recorded.
verify: Compare the recorded segment sizes against the planned channel volumes.
Pass when no planned channel activity exceeds its segment size.

steps.title: Log every challenge raised with an accept, adjust, or defer decision
sop: Log each challenge raised by distribution or product as a separate entry.
Record a decision of accept, adjust, or defer against each challenge with the rationale.
Assign an owner and date to any challenge that requires rework.
Done when every challenge carries a decision and rationale.
verify: Filter the challenge log for entries without a decision.
Pass when the filter returns no entries.

steps.title: Obtain written sign-off from distribution and product leads
sop: Send the validation record with the dispositioned challenges to both leads for written sign-off.
Hold release of the segmentation for targeting until both sign-offs are received.
File the signed record against the segmentation model version.
Done when both written sign-offs are held and filed.
verify: Check the filed record contains explicit approval from distribution and from product.
Pass when the Marketing Manager confirms both sign-offs are on file.

generic.Defined scope/population: Macro, regulatory, and catastrophe exposure trends for the in-scope geographies and lines.
generic.In-scope period: The current planning cycle with indicator history covering the agreed trailing periods.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every cited figure carries a source, publication date, and retrieval date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Number of lines assessed matches the in-scope line list agreed in the scope note.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Source extracts and the assessment retained with retrieval dates and a version stamp.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Trends with insufficient evidence logged and marked as low confidence rather than dropped.
generic.Test population: The completed external trend impact assessment for the current cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every line has a demand direction and confidence level and every figure is sourced.
generic.Exception handling path: Market Research Analyst downgrades confidence or removes the claim when sourcing fails.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Assessment produced with demand direction and confidence per line of business.
generic.Evidence location: Trend assessment workbook in SharePoint with dated source extracts archived beside it.

steps.title: Pull macro indicators for the in-scope geographies into Excel
sop: Pull GDP growth, employment, housing starts, vehicle sales, and construction activity for the in-scope geographies.
Record the source, publication date, and retrieval date beside every series.
Save the dated source extract alongside the workbook.
Done when every macro indicator is loaded with its source metadata.
verify: Check each macro series carries source, publication date, and retrieval date.
Pass when no series is missing any of the three metadata fields.

steps.title: Summarise pending regulatory and rate environment changes by state
sop: Summarise pending regulatory and rate environment changes by state or region.
Note the lines of business each change affects and the expected effective date.
Cite the filing, bulletin, or publication for every change listed.
Done when the regulatory summary covers every in-scope state with citations.
verify: Check each listed change names an affected line and carries a citation.
Pass when no change is listed without both an affected line and a citation.

steps.title: Summarise catastrophe exposure trend signals affecting appetite
sop: Summarise wildfire, wind, flood, and severe convective storm exposure trend signals.
Note where the trend affects appetite as well as where it affects customer demand.
Cite the source and as-of date for each catastrophe signal.
Done when all four peril groups are summarised with sources.
verify: Check each peril group has a summary and a cited source.
Pass when no peril group is left without a sourced summary.

steps.title: Translate each trend into a demand impact per line of business
sop: Translate each macro, regulatory, and catastrophe trend into a directional demand impact per line.
State the direction as increase, decrease, or neutral rather than in narrative only.
Attach a confidence level to each impact based on the strength of evidence.
Done when every in-scope line has a direction and confidence for each relevant trend.
verify: Check the impact table has a direction and confidence for each line and trend pair.
Pass when no cell in the impact table is left blank.

steps.title: Review the impact assessment with the Customer Insights Lead
sop: Review the directional impacts and challenge any judgement not supported by the evidence.
Downgrade the confidence level where the supporting evidence is thin.
Record the review outcome and any changes made.
Done when the review is complete and confidence levels are agreed.
verify: Check every downgraded or challenged impact shows the resulting change.
Pass when the Customer Insights Lead accepts the final confidence levels.

steps.title: Publish the trend assessment to the market intelligence workspace
sop: Publish the assessment with the impact table and the source register to SharePoint.
Version and date the assessment so later cycles can be compared to it.
Link the assessment from the current market briefing page.
Done when the assessment is published, versioned, and linked.
verify: Open the published assessment and check the source register resolves for a sample of figures.
Pass when every sampled figure traces to a dated source in the register.

generic.Defined scope/population: All lines of business and states in scope for the quarterly growth and rate analysis.
generic.In-scope period: The latest completed quarter plus the trailing four quarters for trend comparison.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Written premium, earned premium, and filed rate change populated per line and state.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Written and earned premium totals reconcile to the finance reported figures for the quarter.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Analysis workbook and filing extracts retained with the quarter and retrieval date stamped.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Lines diverging from market beyond threshold logged with the explanation recorded.
generic.Test population: The quarterly line-of-business growth and rate analysis for the current quarter.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when growth decomposes into rate, exposure, and new business and totals reconcile.
generic.Exception handling path: Market Research Analyst refers unexplained divergence to the Data Analyst for source review.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Quarterly analysis produced with decomposition and market comparison per line.
generic.Evidence location: Analysis workbook in SharePoint with the BI growth report and filing extracts attached.

steps.title: Refresh written and earned premium growth by line in the BI platform
sop: Refresh written and earned premium by line of business for the latest quarter.
Add the trailing four quarters so the trend is visible alongside the current period.
Record the data as-of date on the report.
Done when the premium growth report is refreshed for all in-scope lines.
verify: Reconcile the report premium totals to the finance reported figures for the quarter.
Pass when the totals agree within the agreed tolerance.

steps.title: Pull filed and approved rate changes from the regulatory filing portal
sop: Pull filed and approved rate change percentages by line and state from the filing portal.
Record the filing reference and approval date for each rate change captured.
Supplement with industry rate survey figures where filings are unavailable.
Done when rate changes are captured for every in-scope line and state.
verify: Check each captured rate change carries a filing reference or survey citation.
Pass when no rate change is recorded without a source reference.

steps.title: Compare our rate change against the market average per line
sop: Compare our filed rate change per line and state against the market average.
Quantify the gap in percentage points rather than describing it qualitatively.
Highlight lines where we sit materially above or below the market.
Done when the rate gap is quantified for every in-scope line and state.
verify: Recompute the gap for a sample of line and state cells.
Pass when the sampled recomputations match the reported gaps.

steps.title: Decompose growth into rate, exposure, and new business components
sop: Split premium growth per line into rate, exposure, and new business contributions.
Check the three components sum back to the reported total growth for each line.
Record the method used for the decomposition in the workbook.
Done when every line has a complete and balancing decomposition.
verify: Sum the three components per line and compare to the reported growth.
Pass when the components reconcile to total growth for every line.

steps.title: Explain lines diverging from market growth beyond the threshold
sop: Identify lines where our growth diverges from market growth by more than the agreed threshold.
Write the explanation for each divergence using the decomposition and rate gap.
Refer divergences that cannot be explained from the data for further source review.
Done when every threshold divergence has a written explanation or an open referral.
verify: Check each flagged divergence has an explanation or a logged referral.
Pass when no flagged divergence is left with neither.

steps.title: Publish the quarterly analysis to the market intelligence workspace
sop: Assemble the growth, rate gap, and decomposition outputs into the quarterly analysis pack.
Stamp the pack with the quarter, data as-of date, and version.
Publish the pack and link it from the quarterly briefing page.
Done when the pack is published and linked for the current quarter.
verify: Open the published pack and check the quarter, as-of date, and version are stamped.
Pass when all three stamps are present and the linked report opens.

generic.Defined scope/population: The lines of business, geographies, and channels covered by market intelligence this cycle.
generic.In-scope period: The current planning cycle with interim and final delivery dates on the planning calendar.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every priority question carries a requesting executive, evidence standard, and delivery date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Question count in the published scope note matches the questions raised and accepted.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned and dated scope note retained with the stakeholder acknowledgement thread.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Questions excluded from scope logged with the reason and the deciding executive.
generic.Test population: The published market intelligence scope note for the current planning cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every question has a named requester, an evidence standard, and a delivery date.
generic.Exception handling path: Market Research Analyst reissues the scope note when a stakeholder disputes the scope.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Scope note published with prioritised questions, named requesters, and delivery dates.
generic.Evidence location: Scope note in SharePoint with the Confluence workspace page and acknowledgement emails.

steps.title: Collect priority questions from leadership in Teams sessions
sop: Run sessions with leadership to collect the questions market intelligence must answer this cycle.
Record each question separately with the requesting executive named.
Capture why the answer matters so priority can be judged later.
Done when the question list is captured with a named requester on each entry.
verify: Check each captured question names a requesting executive.
Pass when no question is recorded without a named requester.

steps.title: Agree the lines, geographies, and channels in scope
sop: Agree which lines of business, geographies, and channels the intelligence will cover.
Record what is deliberately excluded so expectations are managed.
Confirm the scope is achievable with the available data and team capacity.
Done when the in-scope and excluded lists are recorded.
verify: Check the scope statement covers lines, geographies, and channels explicitly.
Pass when both the in-scope and excluded lists are populated.

steps.title: Agree the evidence standard for acceptable sources
sop: Agree which industry sources, statutory filings, and surveys count as acceptable evidence.
State the treatment for figures that can only be sourced from a single provider.
Record the evidence standard in the scope note draft.
Done when the evidence standard is written into the draft.
verify: Check the evidence standard names specific acceptable source types.
Pass when the standard is specific enough to test a source against.

steps.title: Set interim and final delivery dates against the planning calendar
sop: Map the required outputs against the planning calendar milestones.
Set interim and final delivery dates for each output.
Flag any question that cannot be answered within the calendar and propose deferral.
Done when every output has interim and final dates or a deferral proposal.
verify: Check each output has a delivery date or a recorded deferral.
Pass when no output is left without a date or deferral decision.

steps.title: Prioritise the questions and record exclusions
sop: Rank the questions by decision impact and the delivery date they support.
Record any question excluded from this cycle with the reason and the deciding executive.
Confirm the ranked list fits the team capacity for the cycle.
Done when the prioritised list and exclusions are recorded.
verify: Check every excluded question carries a reason and a deciding executive.
Pass when no exclusion is recorded without both.

steps.title: Publish the scope note and confirm stakeholder acknowledgement
sop: Publish the scope note with questions, requesters, evidence standard, scope, and dates.
Send the note to every requesting executive and ask for acknowledgement.
Chase any acknowledgement not received by the stated date.
Done when the note is published and all acknowledgements are received.
verify: Check the acknowledgement thread covers every named requester.
Pass when the Marketing Manager confirms all requesters have acknowledged.

generic.Defined scope/population: Market direct written and earned premium by line of business and state in the agreed scope.
generic.In-scope period: The current reporting period plus the trailing three years of market growth rates.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every line and state cell carries a premium figure or an explained unavailable marker.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Line and state premium figures sum to the published market totals for each state.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Dated source extracts archived alongside the assembled dataset for reproducibility.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Suppressed or unavailable market cells logged with the reason rather than left blank.
generic.Test population: The assembled market size dataset for the current period.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every material figure is cross-checked against two sources and no cell is blank.
generic.Exception handling path: Market Research Analyst records the unavailable marker and notes the affected analysis.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Market size dataset assembled by line and geography with dated source extracts archived.
generic.Evidence location: Market dataset in the lakehouse with the source extract archive in SharePoint.

steps.title: Extract statutory market share data from the regulatory filing portal
sop: Extract statutory market direct written and earned premium by line and state.
Record the extract date and the source report reference for each extract.
Save the raw extract unaltered before any transformation.
Done when the statutory extracts are saved for every in-scope state.
verify: Check an extract file exists for every in-scope state with a retrieval date.
Pass when no in-scope state is missing its extract.

steps.title: Assemble market premium by line and state in Excel
sop: Load the extracts into the market dataset structure keyed by line and state.
Standardise line of business naming so sources align to our line taxonomy.
Record the mapping applied between source line names and our taxonomy.
Done when the dataset holds premium by line and state on our taxonomy.
verify: Sum line premium by state and compare to the published state total.
Pass when the state totals reconcile to the published figures.

steps.title: Add trailing three-year market growth rates to the dataset
sop: Add market growth rates for the trailing three years alongside the current period figures.
Calculate growth on a consistent basis across all lines and states.
Record the basis used so later periods are computed the same way.
Done when growth rates exist for every populated line and state cell.
verify: Recompute a sample of growth rates from the underlying premium figures.
Pass when the sampled recomputations match the dataset values.

steps.title: Cross-check material figures against a second independent source
sop: Cross-check each material market size figure against a second independent source.
Investigate and resolve differences beyond the agreed tolerance.
Record which source was adopted and why where sources disagree.
Done when every material figure has a second-source check recorded.
verify: Check the cross-check log covers every figure marked material.
Pass when no material figure lacks a second-source check.

steps.title: Flag and document unavailable or suppressed market cells
sop: Identify every line and state cell where market data is unavailable or suppressed.
Mark the cell with an explicit unavailable marker rather than leaving it blank.
Record the reason and the effect on any analysis relying on that cell.
Done when no cell is blank without an unavailable marker and reason.
verify: Scan the dataset for blank cells without markers.
Pass when the scan returns no unexplained blank cells.

steps.title: Archive the dated source extracts with the assembled dataset
sop: Archive every source extract with its retrieval date beside the assembled dataset.
Record the mapping and transformation steps applied from extract to dataset.
Confirm another analyst could reproduce the dataset from the archive.
Done when the archive and the reproduction notes are stored together.
verify: Trace one dataset figure back through the archive to its source extract.
Pass when the traced figure reproduces exactly from the archived extract.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every recommended action arising from the market briefing review with leadership.
generic.In-scope period: The planning cycle the briefing supports, with actions dated against its milestones.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Owner, target date, and acting team populated on every logged action.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Action count in the log matches the actions minuted in the briefing review.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Dated action log retained in the workspace with the circulation record attached.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Actions declined during the review logged with the reason and the deciding leader.
generic.Test population: The action log produced from the current market briefing review.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Pass when every action has a single named owner and a target date, with none unowned.
generic.Exception handling path: Market Research Analyst returns unowned actions to the Marketing Manager for assignment.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Action log complete with owner, due date, and acting team on every entry.

steps.title: Extract the recommended actions from the briefing minutes
sop: Read the briefing minutes and extract every recommendation agreed during the review.
Create one log entry per action rather than bundling related items together.
Write each action in language that states what will actually be done.
Done when every minuted recommendation exists as a separate log entry.
verify: Compare the log entry count against the recommendations in the minutes.
Pass when every minuted recommendation appears as a log entry.

steps.title: Assign a single named owner to each action
sop: Assign one named owner to each action rather than a team name.
Confirm each owner accepts the action before it is recorded as assigned.
Escalate any action no owner accepts back to the review chair.
Done when every action carries an accepted named owner.
verify: Filter the log for entries without a named owner.
Pass when the filter returns no entries.

steps.title: Set target dates aligned to the planning cycle
sop: Set a target date for each action aligned to the planning cycle milestones.
Check the date is achievable with the owner before recording it.
Flag actions whose date falls after the cycle closes for reprioritisation.
Done when every action carries an agreed target date.

steps.title: Classify each action by the acting team

Group the log by team so each team can see its own actions.

Pass when no free-text team value appears in the log.

steps.title: Circulate the action log to attendees within two business days
sop: Circulate the action log to every review attendee within two business days of the session.
Ask attendees to correct any misstated action or ownership by a stated date.
Apply corrections received and reissue the log where material changes are made.

steps.title: Carry open actions forward to the next quarterly briefing agenda
sop: Add every open action to the next quarterly briefing agenda for status update.

generic.Defined scope/population: All briefings, source extracts, datasets, and market assumptions held in the archive.

steps.title: File the quarter's briefings, extracts, and datasets into the archive

Apply the agreed naming convention covering quarter, line of business, and topic.
Confirm no working copy is left outside the archive on a personal drive.
Done when every item from the quarter is filed under the naming convention.
verify: Compare the filed item list against the quarter's output list.
Pass when every produced output has a matching archive item.

steps.title: Update the assumptions register with changed market assumptions
